title: Muscle Pain

rationale.BMP / UA / Ca / Phos: AKI, hyperK, hyperP, hypoCa. UA: blood+, no RBCs.
rationale.Treat hyperkalemia: Calcium gluconate, insulin+glucose, bicarb if severe.

hpi: {{patient_name}} presents with diffuse muscle pain, weakness, dark cola-colored urine (myoglobinuria), and fatigue following prolonged immobilization, crush injury, extreme exertion, or medication reaction. Labs: markedly elevated CK (often >5,000, can be >100,000), elevated Cr (AKI from myoglobin), hyperkalemia, hyperphosphatemia, hypocalcemia. UA positive for blood on dipstick but no RBCs on microscopy (myoglobinuria). Rhabdomyolysis = skeletal muscle breakdown → release of intracellular contents (K, phosphate, myoglobin, CK) into bloodstream. Biggest risk: acute kidney injury from myoglobin pigment nephropathy. Management: AGGRESSIVE IV crystalloid resuscitation (NS or LR, 1-2L bolus then 200-300 mL/hr titrated to urine output >200-300 mL/hr). Monitor urine output, renal function, electrolytes (hyperkalemia → cardiac arrhythmia). Alkalinization with bicarb generally NOT recommended. Treat underlying cause.
